title: The Keys of the Kingdom
definition: The Keys of the Kingdom refer to the Church's Christ-given responsibility to confess the Gospel, receive believers, and exercise discipline according to His Word.
summary: The Keys of the Kingdom describe the authority Christ gives His Church to confess the Gospel, recognize true profession, and exercise discipline.
christFocus: Jesus Christ holds all authority and gives His Church responsibility to confess and guard the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on church authority under Christ. The keys are not independent power but delegated responsibility to affirm the Gospel, receive credible professions, and correct what contradicts Christ's name. It connects doctrine, membership, ordinances, and discipline.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because churches must not treat Gospel identity as shapeless or private. Christ gives His Church responsibility to say, according to Scripture, what belongs to the kingdom and what denies it. Misusing this authority either becomes tyranny or neglect.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Respect church authority when it is exercised biblically and humbly. Leaders should handle the keys with fear of Christ, not personal control. Members should care that the church's confession matches the Gospel.
